question.value: Characterize the physical properties and molecular gas content of four serendipitous CO emitters detected in a blind line search around the SMG SSA22-AzTEC26.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present serendipitous detections and physical properties of four CO emitters in the vicinity of the bright submillimeter galaxy (SMG) SSA22-AzTEC26 from ALMA band 3 observations.

The ALMA band 3 spectral scan observations (Project ID: 2019.1.01102.S; PI: Umehata) were conducted from 2020 March 20 to 2020 April 3, toward the sky position of SSA22-AzTEC26 (R.A. 22:17:13.34, decl. 00:26:51.66).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.01102.S and #2021.1.01207.S.
We also include band 4 and band 7 data (Project ID: 2021.1.01207.S; PI: Umehata) in our analysis.

The velocity-integrated fluxes are measured by fitting a 2D Gaussian profile to the zeroth-moment map, which sums along the spectral axis over a velocity range $\pm$FWHM from the line center.

analysis_steps.goal: Determine photometric redshifts, identify spectral lines, and fit UV-to-FIR SEDs

method.value: Model UV-to-FIR SEDs using Prospector methodology implemented with CIGALE models and EAZY to get photometric redshift PDFs, match with candidate CO/[CI] transitions to get spectroscopic redshifts, then refit SEDs at fixed z_CO including ALMA continuum fluxes.

evidence.quote: We adopt the methodology of `prospector` (cite: 2019ApJ...877..140L) to model the observed spectral energy distribution (SED), which fits all physical parameters simultaneously and yields the joint PDF as a result.

To implement the modification, SED models are built with the `CIGALE` code (cite: 2019A&A...622A.103B). Before line identification, we let the redshift vary freely within a flat prior \[0, 8\] (i.e., the photometric redshift mode of SED fitting).
With the spectroscopic redshift determined from the CO line, we fix the redshift and refit the photometry for galaxies 1, 2, and 4, including band 3, 4, and 7 continuum measurements.

key_parameters.value: Flat priors: beta in [-0.7, 0.4], E(B-V) in [0, 10], redshift z in [0, 8]; SFR averaged over past 30 Myr

analysis_steps.goal: Calculate CO and [CI] line luminosities and derive molecular gas masses

method.value: Convert velocity-integrated line fluxes to line luminosities L' following Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005), convert excited CO to CO(1-0) using normal SFG excitation ratios, and multiply by alpha_CO (and alpha_[CI] for galaxy 1).

evidence.quote: The line luminosity is calculated from the velocity-integrated line flux $S\Delta v$, following (cite: 2005ARA&A..43..677S):

In order to derive their molecular gas mass, we first convert the CO luminosity to the ground transition, assuming line ratios $r_{21}=0.76\pm0.09$ and $r_{31}=0.42\pm0.07$ appropriate for high-redshift normal SFGs (cite: 2015A&A...577A..46D; 2016ApJ...833...70D).

The total molecular gas mass $M_\mathrm{mol}$ is calculated using the conversion factor of normal SFGs: $\alpha_{\mathrm{CO}}=M_\mathrm{mol}/L'_{\mathrm{CO(1-0)}}=$ 3.6 $M_\odot/(\mathrm{K}$ km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2)$; (cite: 2010ApJ...713..686D).

In order to derive their molecular gas mass, we first convert the CO luminosity to the ground transition, assuming line ratios $r_{21}=0.76\pm0.09$ and $r_{31}=0.42\pm0.07$ appropriate for high-redshift normal SFGs (cite: 2015A&A...577A..46D; 2016ApJ...833...70D).
We adopt $X_\mathrm{CI}=10^{-4.8}$ and $Q_{10}=0.35$ following (cite: 2021ApJ...909..181L).

assumptions.value: Normal SFG CO excitation and conversion factor (also tested SMG-like alpha_CO = 1.36, r_21 = 0.84, r_31 = 0.52, X_CI = 10^-4.2, Q_10 = 0.48).

evidence.quote: If we instead assume SMG-like $\alpha_\mathrm{CO}=1.36$ $M_\odot/({\mathrm{K}}$ km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2)$, $r_{21}=0.84\pm0.13$ and $r_{31}=0.52\pm0.09$ (cite: 2013MNRAS.429.3047B), the gas mass will decrease by 2.96 and 3.28 times for CO(2-1) and CO(3-2), respectively.

validation.value: Cross-checked CO-based gas mass of galaxy 1 with [CI](1-0)-based gas mass, gas-to-dust ratio delta_GDR, and L_dust - L'_CO(1-0) relation.

evidence.quote: This translates to a \[CI\](1-0)-based molecular gas mass of $(9.4\pm1.3)\times10^{10}M_\odot$, roughly consistent with the CO-based gas mass.

findings_qualitative.value: Four serendipitous line emitters are detected at S/N > 5.2 in the Band 3 spectral scan cube around SSA22-AzTEC26; two are identified as CO(2-1) at z = 1.113 and 1.146, one as CO(3-2) at z = 2.124 (confirmed by [CI](1-0)), and one remains unconfirmed.

evidence.quote: 1\. Using the photometric redshift, we identify that two of the sources are CO$(2-1)$ at $z=1.113$ and $z=1.146$ respectively. Another is CO(3-2) at $z=2.124$ and confirmed with \[CI\](1-0) emission line detected in the ALMA band 4 observation.

findings_qualitative.value: All three identified CO emitters are massive galaxies (M_star > 10^10.5 M_sun); galaxies 1 and 2 lie on the star-forming main sequence, while galaxy 4 lies significantly below the main sequence yet retains a high molecular gas fraction (~28%).

evidence.quote: 2\. All three sources with a CO redshift solution are massive galaxies ($M_\star>10^{10.5}M_\odot$), with SFR in the order of $\sim1-100$ $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$. Two of them lie within the scatter of the MS and the most massive galaxy 4 is significantly below the MS.
However, the most massive one, galaxy 4, is likely quiescent but maintains a gas ratio of $\sim28\%$, comparable with SFGs on the MS.

findings_qualitative.value: The two blue clumps near galaxy 4 are likely foreground interlopers rather than star-forming clumps or companions associated with the CO emission.

evidence.loc: Relation between Galaxy 4 and the Two Neighboring Sources
evidence.quote: Overall, the positions and properties of the two clumps near galaxy 4 suggest that they are likely to be interlopers rather than companions or parts of the central massive galaxy, from which the CO emission originates.

claims.hypothesis: Blind ALMA Band 3 spectral scans can detect CO emitters spanning a wider range of star formation activity than preselected main-sequence or starburst surveys.
claims.experiment: Smoothed a ~29 GHz bandwidth ALMA Band 3 spectral scan cube around SSA22-AzTEC26 with a 300 km s^-1 Gaussian filter, searched for peaks with S/N > 5.2, and modeled UV-to-FIR SEDs to measure redshifts, stellar masses, SFRs, and gas masses.
claims.result: Detected four line emitters, identifying three massive galaxies (M_star > 10^10.5 M_sun): two CO(2-1) emitters at z = 1.113 and 1.146 and one CO(3-2) emitter at z = 2.124, including one massive quiescent candidate (galaxy 4) significantly below the MS.
claims.finding: Blind CO line searches can detect massive galaxies with low specific star formation rates that still host large gas reservoirs, complementing targeted surveys.

evidence.quote: This shows that a blind CO line search can detect massive galaxies with low specific star formation rates that still host large gas reservoirs and that it also complements targeted surveys

claims.hypothesis: The two blue neighboring clumps around galaxy 4 are foreground interlopers rather than star-forming clumps or gas-rich dwarf companions responsible for the CO(2-1) emission.
claims.experiment: Performed 2D Sersic profile deblending across u-to-K bands, derived photometric redshifts and physical sizes for the central spheroid and two clumps, calculated Roche limits, and checked implied gas-to-stellar mass ratios.
claims.result: Photometric redshifts of the clumps (0.30 and 0.81) disagree with z_CO = 1.146; their sizes (R_e = 0.30'' and 0.35'') exceed the central galaxy (0.16'') while lying inside the Roche limit (1.8''-2.8'') without tidal features; attributing the CO to them implies extreme mu_mol ~ 15-100.
claims.finding: The two blue clumps near galaxy 4 are likely foreground interlopers and the CO(2-1) emission originates from the central massive galaxy.

evidence.loc: Relation between Galaxy 4 and the Two Neighboring Sources
evidence.quote: Overall, the positions and properties of the two clumps near galaxy 4 suggest that they are likely to be interlopers rather than companions or parts of the central massive galaxy, from which the CO emission originates.

claims.hypothesis: The large molecular gas reservoir (M_mol = 6.2 x 10^10 M_sun, mu_mol = 0.28) in the massive quiescent candidate galaxy 4 is simply left over from its main star formation episode.
claims.experiment: Compared galaxy 4's gas fraction, depletion time, and SFH (mass-weighted stellar age 3.3 Gyr, quenching at z ~ 2) against post-starburst gas depletion timescales, morphological quenching limits, and minor merger rates from the Illustris simulation.
claims.result: The >1 Gyr lookback time since quenching exceeds post-starburst gas lifetimes, the 28% gas fraction is too high for morphological quenching alone to halt star formation, and expected minor mergers supply about half the observed gas mass (3.4 x 10^10 M_sun).
claims.finding: The gas reservoir is unlikely to be a simple remnant of past major star formation and was likely acquired at later times, though no single mechanism alone explains both the large gas fraction and low SFR.

evidence.loc: Large Gas Reservoir in a Massive Galaxy below the MS?
evidence.quote: Thus, the gas reservoir in galaxy 4 is no likely to be the remnant of the past major star formation event, but the listed mechanisms might have played a role in maintaining the low SFE.

evidence.loc: Large Gas Reservoir in a Massive Galaxy below the MS?
evidence.quote: We conclude that none of the mechanisms discussed above can explain galaxy 4’s high gas fraction alone, and future high-resolution observations are needed to reveal the nature of galaxy 4.

why_this_data.value: An unbiased blind CO line search in a deep ALMA Band 3 spectral scan with ~29 GHz bandwidth and rich multiwavelength coverage in the SSA22 field avoids preselection biases toward MS or starburst galaxies.

evidence.quote: An unbiased CO survey of galaxies in various stages of star formation is needed to investigate the evolution of gas content before and after galaxy quenching.
The SSA22 field has rich multiwavelength data coverage.

why_this_method.value: Two-component dust attenuation and nonparametric SFH in SED modeling account for complex dust geometry and dust heating by old stars, giving conservative SFR estimates; PSF photometry and 2D Sersic modeling overcome source blending.

evidence.quote: As shown in Figure [3](#fig:fig3), the aperture flux of source 4 is contaminated by two blue neighboring sources. At this moment, we simply assume the two blue sources are foreground galaxies and subtract their contributions using 2D image modeling.
Flux densities are derived from PSF photometry to overcome source blending issues.

evidence.loc: Stellar Mass and SFR from SED Modeling
evidence.quote: Since the dust attenuations of old and young stars are modeled separately and both low and high attenuation values are allowed for the two stellar populations, the error range of SFR$_\mathrm{SED}$ serves as a conservative estimate of the SFR levels.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: SMG-like CO conversion factor (alpha_CO = 1.36) and excitation ratios (r_21 = 0.84, r_31 = 0.52) vs normal SFG conversions: rejected in favor of normal SFG conversions based on the L_dust - L'_CO(1-0) relation for galaxy 1.

evidence.quote: The position of galaxy 1 with respect to the $L_\mathrm{dust}-L^{'}_{\mathrm{CO(1-0)}}$ relation also disfavors a starburst nature of galaxy 1.
In the following discussion, we continue using $M_\mathrm{mol}$ from normal SFG conversions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: UV+IR SFR indicator vs SED-fitted SFR: rejected UV+IR SFR as primary indicator because dust heating by old stars overestimates SFR in low-sSFR galaxies like galaxy 4.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Set line detection threshold at S/N = 5.2 where no negative peaks are found and detection purity reaches 83%; tested filter widths from 100 to 500 km s^-1 and found no additional detections.

evidence.quote: No negative peak is found above S/N$=5.2$.
and determine the free parameters $a=4.72$ and $b=0.71$, which gives a purity of 83% at S/N=5.2. Using this as a detection threshold, we find four sources with S/N$>5.2$ (Figure [2](#fig:fig2)).
We have also tested other filter FWHM values from 100 to 500 km s$^{-1}$ with 100 km s$^{-1}$ steps but do not find any new detection.

limitations_admitted.value: Source 3 has only one line detection in the 29 GHz Band 3 bandwidth and an incompatible NIR photometric redshift, leaving its redshift unconfirmed between z_CO(2-1) = 1.512 and z_CO(3-2) = 2.767.

evidence.quote: Given only one line detection within the $\sim29$ GHz bandwidth, possible solutions will be $z_{\mathrm{CO(2-1)}}=1.512$ or $z_\mathrm{CO(3-2)}=2.767$, but these need to be verified by detecting other spectral lines in future observations (cite: 2014ApJ...781L..39T; 2021ApJ...917...94M).

limitations_admitted.value: Molecular gas mass estimates suffer from substantial uncertainties in alpha_CO and CO excitation ratios.

evidence.quote: We note that molecular gas mass estimates suffer from substantial uncertainties in $\alpha_\mathrm{CO}$ and excitation.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust-based M_mol is poorly constrained due to low S/N (<2) in all Herschel SPIRE bands and uncertainties in dust SED fitting.

evidence.quote: The dust-based $M_\mathrm{mol}$ is the least robust here, because of low S/N ($<2$) in all Herschel bands and the uncertainty in the dust SED fitting (cite: 2016A&A...587A..73B).

limitations_admitted.value: Identification of galaxy 4 as quiescent is tentative because FIR, ALMA continuum, and JVLA 3 GHz upper limits are not deep enough to rule out obscured star formation up to ~220-294 M_sun yr^-1, and optical/NIR spectroscopy is lacking.

evidence.quote: We caution that the current identification of galaxy 4 as a QG is only tentative. The assertion of the low SFR is based on very faint rest-frame UV fluxes and the obscured SFR of galaxy 4 is left not well constrained.
Obviously, current FIR and radio data are not deep enough to constrain galaxy 4’s SFR.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-line CO identifications for galaxies 2 and 4 rely entirely on photometric redshifts without secondary spectral line confirmations.
Applying a normal SFG CO-to-H2 conversion factor (alpha_CO = 3.6) and excitation ratio (r_21 = 0.76) to galaxy 4 may not be valid if it is genuinely a massive quiescent galaxy.
The low random alignment probability (1.18e-3, 3.2 sigma) of the two blue clumps around galaxy 4 leaves open the possibility that they are physically associated at z = 1.146 in an interacting system.

reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project codes, calibrators, spectral setups, line search algorithm, multiwavelength flux tables (Table 1 and Table 2), and SED fitting priors are clearly documented, allowing full reproduction of the line detection, SED modeling, and gas mass calculations once cubes are imaged; however, some tclean parameters and two private-communication ancillary datasets are not publicly provided.
